The ingredients section on this toothpaste tube explains where each ingredient comes from and what it does

explains where each ingredient comes from

No it doesn't. Not in any meaningful way at least, and in some cases it's so vague that it is practically lying.

The world of product packaging is incredibly shady, and the word "natural" is almost always complete and total bullshit.

For instance, the Sodium monofluorophosphate in your toothpaste did not come from fluorspar. Unless, of course, the folks at Kingfisher are fucking alchemists, because you don't get phosphorous from sodium flouride. So, why did they ignore what is the vast majority, in terms of both mass and volume, of the additive that they actually put in their product? Because it's bulk phosphates, which means phosphoric acid. Now, in a real sense that's still "natural" because phosphoric acid is ultimately derived from apatite and sulfuric acid, which is itself derived from sulfur, and I think we can all agree that shit you dig out of the ground is "natural". The problem is that sulfuric and phosphoric acids aren't "natural" in the way that moves toothpaste off shelves and into the homes of "product conscious" consumers.

If you bought that toothpaste because it is "natural" or because it provides "transparent" or "educational" labelling, you got taken.

IT would be interesting for all products to be labeled in a similar manner, with oversight to ensure the claims are concise and true. So tell me that E954 is Sacccharin, its used as an artificial sweetener and comes from... (somewhere).

It would be instructive and interesting.
